title: Weekly Review: Business Central AL Development – May 17–23, 2026
summary: A weekly curated review of Business Central AL development community posts from May 17 - 23, 2026, covering AI-driven developer tooling, security considerations for VS Code extensions, container management automation, agentic development workflows, and release management practices.
key_points: Security risks from VS Code extensions require vetting publishers, permission review, and organizational lock-down to prevent backdoors in development environments
MCP servers enable GitHub Copilot to manage BC containers directly, replacing manual PowerShell workflows and UI clicks
Near-autonomous AL development pipelines can handle 12 stages with 3 human checkpoints, using AI agents for mechanical tasks while humans maintain architectural judgment
Global memory configuration in VS Code agents preserves coding preferences and conventions across workspaces, reducing repetitive instruction
BC major releases frequently pause or postpone during rollout, requiring flexible update schedules and proactive customer communication
